GATES.name: React: Date and month picker
GATES.does: Checks trigger names, grid roles, one tab stop, arrow and page navigation, bounds, blocked periods, and range order. Checks current-period names and rejects legends or cell swatches. Every rendered focusable part must match a kit ring selector.
blind: JSDOM renders no paint: the ring's visibility, the grid's alignment, pointer target sizes and the phone sheet's layout are read as CSS text or left to browser captures, and spoken screen-reader output is not measured.

GATES.name: React: Success
GATES.does: Checks heading ranks including the clamp on out-of-range levels, polite status markup, hidden artwork with no backdrop layer, the omitted empty actions row, both check marks and the fallback for an unknown one, the bare shared mark and its wrappers, keyboard action access, refs, axe results and cancelable countdown ownership, including StrictMode.
blind: JSDOM cannot measure paint, colour contrast, real layout or actual screen-reader announcements.

GATES.name: Scroll region focus
GATES.does: Resolves source CSS in JSDOM with forced focus state. Checks six scroll regions in two themes and two accents. Each region draws no resting outline, then takes the shared inward outline and offset. Ancestor paint stays unchanged. Coverage counts and missing-rule, offset and transparent-outline mutations prove rejection.
blind: JSDOM cannot prove scrolling, real keyboard reachability, clipping or rendered outline survival during scrolling. Those require separate browser checks.
Historical captures reported on #531 are unverified in this audit. They are not proof for the current head or proof of keyboard behavior.
React modal-body source coverage belongs to react/src/focus-ring.test.tsx.

GATES.name: Inline link focus
GATES.does: Renders every story the vanilla catalogue exports, collects every anchor they draw, and resolves the kit's focus rules over each one by specificity and document order: a link has to draw var(--ring) on :focus-visible, never the browser's own outline and never an outline of its own beside it. Counts the stories rendered, the stories that draw a link and the links judged, so a catalogue that stopped drawing links could not leave it green. Deletes the element-wide rule from the sheet it lives in and requires the walk to go red, and judges the four verdicts one declaration apart on a fixture link.
blind: The source resolver models specificity and source order. It does not model !important, inline styles, query conditions, other interaction states or token expansion.
The accessibility-floor gate calculates ring contrast from source colours. Neither gate measures browser pixels.
Only the vanilla catalogue, and only markup a story renders synchronously: a link a script adds after render is unwalked, and React's anchors are judged in react/src/focus-ring.test.tsx.
Line wrapping is not measured. A link split across lines needs a separate browser check of its focus outline.

GATES.name: Snippet focus
GATES.does: Discovers fourteen focusable targets in Snippet fixtures. In both themes and two accents, checks that the shared outline follows the card for a focused code region and follows other controls themselves. Rejects duplicate outlines and focus shadows. Checks the declared radius and clipping. Four missing-rule or clipping mutations prove rejection.
blind: JSDOM resolves source styles but cannot prove keyboard reachability, browser clipping or system-colour paint. It evaluates no media query. These require separate browser evidence.
This gate does not assert outline-offset. The ring-carrier gate checks that ring declarations also declare the shared offset.

GATES.name: React: Snippet stories
GATES.does: Clicks every React copy button in the Snippet stories and checks the clipboard got the text the code region displays, pairs the Comparison story's two columns, and rejects a story whose children drift from its code. Counts the buttons it measured.
blind: jsdom and strings only: no token colour (react/src/contrast.test.tsx) and no layout (browser captures).
The vanilla copy button is unmeasured because wireTopbar() reads innerText, which jsdom does not implement.

GATES.name: React: Chart
GATES.does: Checks the chart's accessible names, the one tab stop inside the plot and the kit ring on every focusable part — including the named scroller around the table, which the sheet rings rather than the browser — arrow/Home/End stepping with its polite announcements, Enter selection and the band behind the picked column with its strong-ink, heavier label, the readout's contents and its Escape behaviour, the whole touch sequence down to the click behind it, where the tap that opens a readout picks nothing and the tap that closes one does, the box every mark offers a pointer and how much of the room around it a line's point may take once a coarse pointer asks for the phone floor, the hollow bar and dash on an unfinished period, the hairline at every tick with the zero rule over them, the flat fill, the one rounded end and the capped width on every bar, the lane two bar series in one band take each, the carry a bridge draws from one step to the next, the ground casing under a line that carries no markers, the table fallback, and axe results in both themes.
blind: JSDOM has no layout, so the readout's placement, the grid's hairline beside the zero rule, the scroll fade and the focus ring are not measured as painted; browser captures cover those. The pointer targets are read off the attributes the component writes, with the media query and the plot's measured width both stubbed, so what a real coarse pointer gets — and whether the table's scroller really overflows a 390px card — is a browser measurement too. Which colour each series takes, and whether it clears the graphic bar, is react/src/Chart.contrast.test.tsx. Screen-reader speech is not run, and no test drives real touch hardware: the sequence is fired as events.

GATES.name: React: Chart contrast
GATES.does: Discovers every chart tone from the stylesheet and every tone name from the component's own union, fails when the two disagree, and measures each tone against both grounds the kit draws a chart on — the card and the page — in both themes and under every accent discovered in accents.css, against the 3:1 graphic bar. Asserts the measured count, names the tightest row, and proves rejection twice: the lighter weight of the accent drawn at the share the restyle's mock used, and a tone whose value stops resolving.
blind: The ratios come from the stylesheet's own values rather than from painted pixels, so antialiasing, a host override and a ground a consumer names through --ui-chart-ground are outside it; browser captures carry the paint.
The grid, the zero rule and the line's casing are structure rather than series — the kit's edge and ground tokens — and are not measured against the bar.

GATES.name: React: Checkbox and radio
GATES.does: Checks accessible labels, pointer and Space activation, controlled radio selection and arrow navigation, disabled inputs, refs, form values, reset and axe results. Measures the 24px box target of every box in a checkbox list with hints, on the markup React renders, in both themes, with the floor gate's geometry.
blind: JSDOM and user-event simulate keyboard behavior; browser paint, hit tests and screen-reader speech need separate checks. The target is read from declared sizes, not laid out.

GATES.name: React: Switch
GATES.does: Checks the accessible name and native checkbox semantics, controlled pointer and keyboard updates, disabled activation, refs, form submission, reset and axe results.
blind: JSDOM does not render the switch track or focus ring, measure contrast, or verify screen-reader speech.

GATES.name: React: Sidebar navigation
GATES.does: Checks named links and counts, current-page semantics, nested keyboard disclosures, disabled rows, router rendering, slots and unique IDs.
blind: JSDOM does not measure CSS, grid alignment, target sizes or spoken screen-reader output.

GATES.name: React: NavTabs
GATES.does: Checks native route-link semantics, current and disabled state, keyboard order, root refs, badge text, safe destinations and axe results. Checks content and container remeasurement without resetting the scroll position.
blind: JSDOM does not measure responsive layout, focus-ring pixels or actual browser navigation. Story contrast and browser captures cover the shared styling.

GATES.name: React: Breadcrumbs
GATES.does: Checks ordered trail semantics, current-page text, ancestor links, decorative icons, keyboard focus, root refs, safe destinations and axe results.
blind: JSDOM does not measure browser layout, visual separators or spoken screen-reader output. Story contrast and browser captures cover shared styling.

GATES.name: React: Tooltip
GATES.does: Checks description IDs, keyboard focus, Escape dismissal, touch toggling, placement and axe results.
blind: Geometry is mocked; browser layout, focus rings and reduced motion need browser checks.

GATES.name: React: Feedback showcase
GATES.does: Checks blank-note prevention, sending and success, cancellation, and the failed note's invalid state, alert and linked error message beside the surviving consent hint, without a false completion announcement.
blind: The send is simulated. JSDOM checks live-region markup and text, not spoken output or browser clearance above toasts. It does not deliver feedback.

GATES.name: React: AppShell
GATES.does: Checks route-derived link names and counts, fold persistence, the search trigger's whole accessible name, search focus and shortcut, account actions, and sheet dismissal.
blind: JSDOM does not measure responsive layout, hover labels, target sizes or rendered contrast.

JSDOM builds a name from contents by joining the spans with no separator, and a browser inserts a space between non-inline children. The search trigger's name is asserted with that one separator matched rather than written, so this gate does not hold which of the two a reader hears.

GATES.name: React: Toast
GATES.does: Checks the polite region, unchanged focus, dismissal timing, action buttons, reduced motion and axe rules with a notice present.
blind: JSDOM does not measure layout, CSS animation or screen reader announcements.

GATES.name: React: Fields
GATES.does: Checks generated label and message links, required and invalid controls, file selection and replacement, drop handling, disabled fields, form reset and axe violations.
blind: JSDOM does not open the system picker or supply a native DataTransfer. The React contrast gate resolves source text colours. Appearance needs browser checks.

GATES.name: React: SearchField
GATES.does: Checks that the toolbar search field renders the vanilla search input group attribute for attribute, is a searchbox named by ariaLabel with no visible label and no clear button, keeps the kit ring on its one focusable part, forwards its ref, className and native input props, and passes axe.
blind: JSDOM checks structure and names. Browser ring paint, row height and screen-reader speech require separate checks. Screenshots cannot prove speech.

GATES.name: React: File drop
GATES.does: Checks the resting row, the picker opened from the button, chosen and dropped files, a drag that carries no file, the target a parent drives, the progress bar's name and value, the uploaded and failed states with their retry and remove actions, and a disabled drop that accepts nothing.
blind: JSDOM does not open the system picker, so the choice is simulated. It does not measure the drop target's cover, the focus ring or contrast, and it reads live-region markup rather than spoken screen-reader output; the kit does not announce the change from uploading to uploaded.

GATES.name: React: Timeline
GATES.does: Checks ordered-list semantics, timestamps, event order, keyboard undo and axe violations.
blind: It does not measure browser layout, colour contrast or screen-reader speech.

GATES.name: React: Tabs
GATES.does: Checks controlled selection, tab and panel links, counts, unique IDs, arrow-key wrapping, Home and End, and keyboard focus into the selected panel.
blind: It does not measure rendered styles or reduced-motion timing in a browser.

GATES.name: React: KeyValueList
GATES.does: Checks definition-list markup, missing or redacted values, native link focus, heading levels, and axe violations.
blind: It does not measure browser wrapping, responsive layout, or contrast in the rendered page.

GATES.name: Ring carrier
GATES.does: Reads both workspaces' stylesheets and holds the focus band to one declaration and one shape: --ring, --ring-offset, --ring-scroll and --ring-scroll-offset are each declared once, at :root, the two bands differ only in which way they are drawn, and none of the four reads a token a painted surface re-points. It then requires every rule that takes a band to take the offset that places it, since a band without its offset is drawn on the border box instead of 1px off it, and holds the consumer count so a control that stops drawing the ring is named. Two tripwires: nothing declares or reads --ring-gap, which #578 retired with the painted gap, and no consumer keeps the transparent 2px outline that stood in for the band under forced colors. Proves rejection four times: the offset dropped from the shared rule in base.css and from the drawer's inward band, and both offset readings run on fixtures as well. Form focus rules use focus-visible.
blind: It reads the sheets as text and measures no pixels: that the band lands 1px out and 2px wide, and what it contrasts against, need Chromium evidence and the contrast ledger.

It asks whether a rule writes the band whole, not whether that rule WINS over the always-on rules on the same element — the focus walk resolves the cascade — and not whether every keyboard stop has a rule at all.
A consumer outside src/ and react/src/ is not read; an example page composes the kit's own classes.

GATES.name: Underline strips fit their column
GATES.does: Under SEG_WRAP=1, drives a browser over every story that renders an underline segmented strip, plus two fixtures carrying the long labels no story has, and reads each strip against its own box at 320, 390 and 1280. No tab is drawn outside the box, no tab is wider than the box can hold, the page never scrolls sideways, the strip is not a scroll box clipping the focus outline, and on a wrapped strip the chosen tab's rail is read against the ink of its own label and of the next row's, so it cannot sit close enough to both to read as either row's mark. It holds the issue's own case, the Stock screener's three views on two rows at 390 and one row at 1280, and re-runs every check at 320 against four mutations — the sheet put back to one row and a scroll box, the rows closed to the track's own gap, and the tab label put back to `nowrap` and to `break-word` — all of which have to fail.
blind: The measuring half is off unless SEG_WRAP=1, because Playwright is deliberately not a dependency of this package, so CI runs nothing here and the measurement is reported by hand in the pull request.
One engine and one theme. Firefox and Safari are not measured here, and neither is the ring's rendered contrast, which belongs to the contrast ledger.
It sweeps stories/ only, so no React strip is measured. React's Segmented emits the same markup against the same sheet, so it moves with it by construction, but nothing here holds that.

Every subject the sweep discovers has a label of one or two short words. A tab that cannot fit its column at all is shown only by the two fixtures beside them, so if those are dropped the containment checks go green against the defect they were written for.
It reads geometry and never paint. A strip whose tabs all fit while being illegible, mis-coloured or wrongly ordered passes every check in this file.

GATES.name: React: BackLink
GATES.does: Checks the React back link against the factory rule: the arrow is aria-hidden so its meaning is spoken in words; the accessible name includes the visible text as WCAG 2.5.3 requires; and a name already saying "Back to" is not repeated.
blind: Whether the link is reachable in its location. It is a static anchor with no state, so this gate does not press a key. The shell gate places it on a page.

GATES.name: React: Dropdown
GATES.does: Simulates keyboard input in JSDOM. Checks opening focus, arrow movement, disabled rows, Home, End, Enter, Space, Escape, Tab and closing focus. Search keeps focus in the combobox and links the active row. Checks row roles and selection attributes against the factory.
blind: Whether requested focus lands. JSDOM moves focus into a box hidden by the stylesheet. The rule that makes an opening panel visible when the key lands is checked by the overlay CSS gate against the stylesheet.
A caller’s row is accessible only if the caller spreads the props onto the correct element. This gate checks that props arrive, not where a consumer spreads them.

GATES.name: React: Pagination
GATES.does: Checks where focus goes when a pager step becomes disabled at an end or during loading, and ensures the jump box never commits a page the reader did not request.
blind: Real browser focus. JSDOM does not blur a control that becomes disabled, so tests simulate the move to `<body>`.

GATES.name: Palette keyboard
GATES.does: Dispatches keyboard events in JSDOM. Checks opening shortcuts, active-row movement, Enter, top-overlay Escape, the Tab trap, and live-region text.
blind: Whether requested focus lands. As with the drawer gate, JSDOM has no layout or transition, so a focus() that a browser would reject is counted as successful.
The pointer. Hovering changes the active row and clicking runs it; this gate does neither.

GATES.name: Command palette
GATES.does: Checks the palette guidelines against the component: its keyboard contract matches the keys the sources compare, its grouping uses the claimed label role, and every rendered palette row goes somewhere, runs something, asks something or says it is unavailable.
blind: What a key does. It checks which keys are handled, not the result; the palette keyboard gate presses them.
A row a story does not render. The sweep is the catalogue, so a product’s own palette is covered only where the kit renders it.

GATES.name: The page
GATES.does: Renders app stories and checks page structure, heading order, named navigation landmarks with distinct names, shell order, and initially closed overlays. It also checks page limits and their documentation references.
blind: CSS behaviour. It reads story markup without resolving stylesheets, so display:none content is still a heading and an off-screen landmark is still present.
What headings say. A correct rank and an incorrect title look the same here; the letter-case gate checks the words.
A screen no story draws. The sweep covers only the story app screens, so a consumer page is covered only to the extent that the kit draws the same shape.

GATES.name: Contrast (dark)
GATES.does: Resolves source colours for text-owning elements in rendered vanilla stories, in the dark theme, against the background composited above it. Split from one combined file so each theme's walk stays inside its own time budget (#562); stories/contrast-light.test.js is the light half and carries the self-checks that do not depend on a theme.
blind: Layout, including a toast over the page, a dropdown over a card or a drawer over its scrim. DOM ancestry stands in for visual stacking and is wrong where the two differ. This is the gate’s largest gap; only a browser closes it (#131).
Paint layers the walk cannot see, such as a ::before backdrop or sibling glow. Nine pairs per backdrop are judged against the wrong ground.
Gradients and images an element owns or inherits. These are reported as unjudgeable, not passed.
Filters. .ui-btn--primary:hover brightens, but the gate reads the pre-filter colour.
Inactive components and everything inside them. This is the gap filled by this page’s third number.
Non-text contrast such as borders, focus rings and icon strokes, which requires geometry.
More than one accent and any state beyond hover, focus-visible, focus and active.

GATES.name: Contrast (light)
GATES.does: Resolves source colours for text-owning elements in rendered vanilla stories, in the light theme, against the background composited above it. The other half of the split in stories/contrast-dark.test.js (#562); this file also carries the toast, success-panel and chip self-checks that run once over both themes because they do not depend on either theme's walk.
blind: Layout, including a toast over the page, a dropdown over a card or a drawer over its scrim. DOM ancestry stands in for visual stacking and is wrong where the two differ. This is the gate’s largest gap; only a browser closes it (#131).
Paint layers the walk cannot see, such as a ::before backdrop or sibling glow. Nine pairs per backdrop are judged against the wrong ground.
Gradients and images an element owns or inherits. These are reported as unjudgeable, not passed.
Filters. .ui-btn--primary:hover brightens, but the gate reads the pre-filter colour.
Inactive components and everything inside them. This is the gap filled by this page’s third number.
Non-text contrast such as borders, focus rings and icon strokes, which requires geometry.
The default run uses one accent. CONTRAST_ACCENTS=1 enables both themes under each alternate accent. States beyond hover, focus-visible, focus and active remain unmeasured.

GATES.name: A11y
GATES.does: Runs axe over every story in both themes for WCAG 2.0/2.1 A and AA. It asserts that the check count equals stories × themes so nothing disappears silently.
blind: Accents. It uses only the default accent in two themes; testing every accent repaints tokens and costs runtime.
color-contrast, deliberately. Axe cannot resolve var() in a headless DOM and would treat the kit tokens as having no colour.
Anything static markup cannot show. Axe passed a tablist that controlled nothing.

GATES.name: Keyboard
GATES.does: Dispatches keyboard events in JSDOM to wired segmented controls and tabs. Checks roving tab stops, arrow wrapping, Home and End, panel selection, and field naming, required and invalid attributes.
blind: Synthetic events and DOM focus do not prove browser keyboard behavior. Other components require their separate gates.

GATES.name: Drawer separators and footer
GATES.does: Discovers drawer panels in every story in both themes, checks header and group separators and an unfilled footer without a rule, and rejects deliberately broken specimens.
blind: Footer fill is compared with the panel surface; text contrast, rendered spacing, shadows and pseudo-elements are not measured.

GATES.name: Dashboard references
GATES.does: Drives the links between the kit's dashboard and the report behind it in JSDOM, in both frames a story can be looked at from, and reads back what each click arrives at: that the row the reference names is marked, brought to the middle of the view and never sideways, and given the keyboard, so a screen reader arrives on the row with the reader rather than at the top of the report.
blind: Historical browser captures, manual checks and browser measurements mentioned in this entry were not authenticated in this audit. They do not prove this head.
No layout and no paint. JSDOM ships no scrollIntoView, so what is held is the ask and not where the row lands on a screen; a browser run in the pull request carries that, at 1280, 390 and 320.
Not whether a screen reader announces the row it was moved to. What is read is document.activeElement, which is markup, not speech.

Not the Storybook manager. That selecting a story keeps the manager's globals, and so the theme, is Storybook's own behaviour; this only holds that the click asks the manager to select the story instead of replacing the frame with a bare preview URL, which is what dropped the theme.

GATES.name: Drawer focus
GATES.does: Checks that opening the drawer requests focus inside its panel.
blind: Whether focus really lands. JSDOM has no CSS or transitions, and the original bug involved transitioned visibility making focus() a no-op in Chrome. This gate can prove only the request.

GATES.name: Accent contrast
GATES.does: Checks a token contract across all eight theme × accent cells. It renders nothing, runs in milliseconds and sees pairs no story happens to render.
blind: Anything a component composes that the tokens do not state alone.

GATES.name: Inline code: the chip's surface
GATES.does: Discovers opaque grounds, callout washes and all thirteen badge and pill fills from the sheets. Composites each layer over every ground in both themes and each discovered token context. Requires a 1.1:1 code-chip step except for the two named tinted-card cases. Checks coverage counts, readable colours, explicit handoffs, and that the chip paints its inherited surface without an edge or its own focus ring.
blind: Source colour composition only, with no browser pixels, layout or nested text contrast. Browser evidence requires a separate run. One ground per selector, the last declared; one accent. Layers outside callout.css and badge.css are not measured. Two light tinted cards remain below the floor with a written reason.

GATES.name: Elevation
GATES.does: Checks every box-shadow declared by the kit’s stylesheets, reads each layer’s geometry per theme and rejects a cast shadow that is not the floating treatment. It also checks the floor this page needs: --muted on raised surfaces clears AA in both themes.
blind: The rendered result. Ratios are arithmetic over flat colours, while a blurred penumbra is not one. The drop is scored at its core, the darkest ink it lays down.
filter: drop-shadow(). Two shipped cases are zero-offset signal-colour glows; an offset one would pass here unseen.
A shadow from markup, such as an inline style in a story or a consumer stylesheet.
A cast appearing only when two custom properties simultaneously have non-winning values. Each name is tested against every kit value, one at a time.

GATES.name: Signal contrast
GATES.does: Reads declarations from the source and checks twenty status-glyph pairs against the stroke-width rule’s bar.
blind: Colour for glyphs without a status. Width is checked next door; ratio is not.

GATES.name: Stat basis
GATES.does: Requires every change shown in a stat band to state its comparison basis in reachable text, either beside the change or in the caption it points to, never only in a hover title.
blind: Whether the named comparison is correct. It checks only that one exists and is reachable.

GATES.name: Glyph stroke
GATES.does: Renders every story and calculates the declared width of every stroked glyph, resolving inheritance and the icon factory’s default, against the stroke-width rule’s 1.5 CSS px line.
blind: Colour. It measures only width; the stroke-width rule determines the relevant bar.
Anything no story renders, so it also rejects a sizing rule without a specimen.
State. Stories render at rest, so a stroke declared only in :hover is unseen.
Widths come from source CSS and SVG attributes. No browser layout or painted stroke pixels are measured.

GATES.name: Accessibility minimums
GATES.does: Pins three page numbers: target size for every rendered control, using its box UNION generated pseudo-elements; ring contrast against every ground; and the composite left by a disabled control. Each disabled control is measured as rendered and again without its disabled attribute, so the pair must change — the ink, the fill and the edge around the box, because a state can be said by the line as well as by the ink. A rule that says it with that line alone is asked about its own box and not about the labels inside it, which are painted by whichever rule paints THEIR ink. Every control in a folded rail is measured separately, with its name read while the label is off-screen.
blind: Historical browser captures, manual checks and browser measurements mentioned in this entry were not authenticated in this audit. They do not prove this head.

A disabled input’s value. The walk measures text nodes, while an input stores its value in a property. Thus .ui-input:disabled is found and repainted but contributes no pair; its tokens are measured on other controls using them.
Width for anything sized by a line of text. It is reported unmeasurable, not passed. An overlay may widen known width but cannot provide one.
The 2.5.8 spacing exception, which is entirely a layout question.
Overlay position. Size is read but offset is not, so both a clear overlay and one covering a neighbour count without that distinction being reported.
Clipping. An overflow:hidden ancestor can cut an overlay, but boxes are not composited here. .ui-toast clips, and its close control was checked by hand.
The ring’s inner edge. Only the outside ground is measured.

What an unavailable edge measures against the ground behind it. The comparison is the state’s own paint against the live one, so a rule changing an edge to an equally faint ink still counts as a repaint. stories/filter-row-edge.test.js resolves which token each box on the filter row draws, and the contrast walk owns the ratios.

GATES.name: Confirm keyboard
GATES.does: Uses the same key-pressing method as the keyboard gate for confirm(): focus enters the question, Escape answers it and Tab cannot leave.
blind: Browser behaviour JSDOM lacks, including transitions, paint and scrolling.

GATES.name: Overlay stack
GATES.does: Checks two overlays open together: who owns Escape, what is inert, where Tab goes and what remains after one closes out of order.
blind: Focus that is requested but does not land, due to the same JSDOM limit as the drawer gate.

GATES.name: Overlay css
GATES.does: Reads drawer, confirm and command-palette stylesheets as text and checks their transition rules, because the broken rules involved transitioned visibility that JSDOM cannot run.
blind: Whether the rule reaches the element. It reads declarations, not the cascade.

GATES.name: Dropdown state chip contrast
GATES.does: Discovers non-live chips in Dropdown stories and measures text at 4.5:1, soft fill separation in both themes, absence of edges and standard badge dimensions. Selected labels and non-status badges use body ink. Missing-fill and border mutations prove rejection.
blind: Browser layout, hover and focus paint, anti-aliasing, and consumer overrides. JSDOM resolves the resting story cascade only.

GATES.name: Badge tone family
GATES.does: Discovers every badge and pill tone from the stylesheet and every accent from accents.css, then requires each fill to leave its ground in one direction — lighter in dark, darker in light — inside a soft separation band, with no edge and ink above 4.5:1 on its own fill. It measures three grounds (the page, a card and a floating panel) under both themes and all four accents, asserts the case count is the product of those three dimensions, and checks the grounds composite to distinct surfaces rather than silently collapsing to one. It names the thirteen tones it expects. Two mutations prove rejection: re-pointing a tone at the opaque card surface, and putting accent ink back on the neutral fill, which fails on a dark floating panel under three accents of four.
blind: Browser layout, anti-aliasing and consumer overrides. This gate, stories/contrast-dark.test.js, stories/contrast-light.test.js and stories/dropdown-state-contrast.test.js resolve source colours in JSDOM. None measures browser pixels. Browser measurements require separate evidence.
Whether a tone is the right one for a status. It measures the paint, not the meaning.
The separation floor on the light page is 1.03 rather than 1.1, because the light glow washes sit close to --bg there: warn and pending measure 1.043 today. Tightening it means moving those alphas.
The 7:1 light-success aim is a written consumer rule only. This gate enforces 4.5:1 and would accept the previous success pair at 5.29:1.

GATES.name: Dropdown field ground
GATES.does: Measures how deeply the dropdown search field sinks into its panel, compared per theme with the kit’s own field on a card. The surrounding surface determines the depth: a floating panel is one level above a card.
blind: Legibility. It checks field ground against its surround, not whether field text clears AA; the contrast walk checks that.
Every other field. It checks one selector in one stylesheet, so a second field added to a panel later is not covered.

GATES.name: Dropdown foot role
GATES.does: Places the same head and foot in each panel dropdown() can emit and runs axe over all three. Thus the rule that a control belongs only in the search variant’s dialog is measured rather than merely documented.
blind: Everything else in the foot. It asks one question of one slot, not about rows, trigger or keyboard.
A control on which axe has no opinion. The rule uses aria-required-children, which counts children by role rather than behaviour.

GATES.name: Dropdown reach
GATES.does: Opens a select in a Modal, a Drawer, a page and a wrapper inside a body, in both kits, and checks that the whole panel, the field's label and the trigger stay in view through End and Escape. In the React half it runs axe's aria-input-field-name rule on the open listbox.
blind: Every other axe rule. It asks only whether the open listbox has a name.
Touch, a real phone, Safari and Firefox. The browser half runs only on request, in Chromium.

GATES.name: Field zoom
GATES.does: Mounts stories without styles and checks whether the touch-zoom selector matches their fields. Reads declarations for the 16px important net. Rejects larger field sizes that the net would shrink, competing important font sizes, and other coarse-pointer field-size rules.
blind: Historical browser captures, manual checks and browser measurements mentioned in this entry were not authenticated in this audit. They do not prove this head.

The cascade. Nothing is resolved; jsdom does not rank !important between rules and would return the component size. Declarations are compared directly. The gate proves only that the net is the kit’s sole important font size, not that a browser resolves it so.
Whether a browser matches (pointer: coarse). jsdom evaluates no media query, and this gate reads the net block as text. The device evidence is the screenshots under the touch-zoom documentation.
Safari’s threshold. 16px is observed browser behaviour, not a standard, so this gate cannot measure the number itself.
Layout. Larger text can grow its box, but no box is laid out. The phone pager strip is a review question, not a gate failure.
A field rendered only by a host page. The selector can reach it, but this walk cannot see it.

GATES.name: Reduced motion
GATES.does: Checks the prefers-reduced-motion net (WCAG 2.3.3). It parses the reduced-motion stylesheet, so deleting one of the net’s !important durations fails. It also fails a duration with !important outside a reduced-motion block, which would override the net; one inside a component block that does more than disable motion; and an !important loop count above one. Finally, it finds every script waiting for animationend or transitionend, including a React onTransitionEnd prop, and requires a timer in the same function. A reduced-motion branch alone does not count.
blind: Which timer is used. Any setTimeout in the function counts, even if unrelated to the listener.
Whether a browser applies the net. jsdom evaluates no media query, so the net is read but never run.
Delays. The net does not zero animation-delay or transition-delay, and this gate does not look for them.
Inline styles written by scripts and script-driven motion such as requestAnimationFrame or element.animate().

GATES.name: Reveal focus
GATES.does: Finds every surface in the kit's sheets that hides itself with visibility: hidden, rather than taking a list, and requires each one to be classified. A surface the kit focuses into is opened with the kit's own wiring, and every element inside it must be reached by a reduced-motion rule that switches transitions off: the net's 0.01ms transition on `all` holds an inherited, discrete visibility at hidden for the tick a focus call happens in, which is #519. A surface holding nothing focusable carries the reason it is exempt instead, and a new one nobody classifies fails the gate.
blind: Whether a browser obeys the rules. jsdom evaluates no media query and runs no transition, so the cover is matched against markup and never run.
Which element the kit focuses. Cover is asked of every element inside an open surface, not of the focus target alone.
A surface hidden by a consumer's own sheet, or a visibility written into an inline style by a script.

GATES.name: Panel ring room
GATES.does: Requires every panel the dropdown wiring opens to leave the kit ring one of its two ways out of a row that fills the panel edge to edge: padding at least what the ring spreads outside the row, read from --ring-gap-width and --ring-width at run time, or no clip at the panel's edge. A panel that pads by nothing and clips as well cuts the ring away, which is what left the account menu's keyboard row with two accent bars instead of a ring in #519; the account menu now takes the second way out and the other two panels the first. Discovers the panels twice and requires the two readings to agree: every place src/ and react/src/ write `data-dropdown-panel` into markup, named by the first class on the marked element itself whichever order the two attributes stand in, against the panels its own fixtures render. A factory that marks a fourth panel is in the first reading and not the second, so it stops the gate until somebody renders and measures it. Proves rejection seven times over: by putting the clip back on the account menu, by showing the same clip passes over a panel that keeps the room, by building that fourth factory in a string, by marking a panel before its own class inside a wrapper whose class the fixtures already measure, and by standing a quoted `//` or `/*` in front of the marker — the comment stripping used to blank the rest of that line and the marker with it, so a clipping panel behind a protocol-relative URL was discovered by nobody (#579), and by standing a regex literal after a control statement's head in front of it — read as division, the `/*` inside that literal opened a comment that blanked the factory below it, so the gate passed every test it had with a panel nobody had measured (#598), and by standing one after a compound head — `else if` and `for await` were read as one word each by a walk that ended no token at whitespace, so their head was no head, and the same literal erased the same factory with all seven tests passing (#598).
blind: Historical browser captures, manual checks and browser measurements mentioned in this entry were not authenticated in this audit. They do not prove this head.
Pixels. The reading is of the stylesheet; it checks that the panel leaves the ring a way out, never that a browser drew the ring. Chrome measured that for #519, before and after, in both themes.
Ancestors. A panel that clips nothing itself can still sit inside something that clips. None of the three does here, and this gate asks the panel.
Anything but the panel's own base rule — padding or overflow a media query adds, and padding on a wrapper between the panel and its rows.
A second class on a marked element — a `panelClass` the caller passes, or a consumer's own. Only the first class is read, because that is the one the panel's own sheet styles it under.

A third way of writing a panel's attributes. The marked element is found by walking the source for tags and attribute lists rather than by parsing it, and a marker it cannot tie to exactly one class attribute stops the gate instead of being named by a neighbour's class.

A fourth shape of comment. Code is told from text by a walk rather than by a parser: a `//` or `/*` inside a string, a template or a regex literal is markup and stays, only a comment is blanked, and source the walk cannot finish — a template, a string or a block comment with no end — stops the gate rather than being read half lexed. Which of a regex literal and a division a `/` opens is read off the code before it: a value divides, and a keyword or a control statement's head does not. A head is read from a fixed list of keywords and the two pairs the language opens one with, `else if` and `for await`; a head the walk did not know would read as a value, and a `/*` inside the regex after it as a comment. A `/` the walk cannot be sure of, which in TSX is the one in `` or after `{...rest}`, costs the stripping of its own line and never the code; an apostrophe in JSX text it takes for a string costs that line too.
A panel hand-written into an example page or a story. The source reading covers src/ and react/src/, the two trees the package ships; those pages compose the factories, which are read.

Whether the rows take the ring at all. `.vopt:focus-visible` never names `.vsw__menu`, so pairing a panel to its rows from selectors alone would be guesswork; the keyboard walk in stories/focus-ring.test.js is what asks every stop for a ring.

Content inserted by innerHTML, and React markup mounted or unmounted without a state class, such as DataTable rows after sorting. React overlays have one, including .rx-scrim.is-open and the kit drawer’s .is-open, and these are read.
Ancestors. The element is matched by its rightmost classes, so a transition under another parent still counts.

GATES.name: Nav cascade

JSDOM ranks author rules faithfully but does not rank by origin. The user-agent boundary is a known exception, documented in the contribution guide’s cascade section.

How large the mark looks to an eye. The step is composited down the ancestor chain and read as a contrast ratio, which is a number and not a perceptual distance — 1.19:1 is ΔL* 8.3 in dark and 1.11:1 is ΔL* 4.2 in light, so the same floor buys less in light. The rail inside the page shell stands on a different ground and is measured in stories/apps/shell-states.test.js; the browser captures on the pull request show both.

GATES.name: Nav long label
GATES.does: In a real browser, renders a current tab with a long route label at 320px and measures that its label start and focus ring stay inside the row. It requires equal background, border, font-family, font-size, line-height, text-align and width. The three font facets are separate because Chrome writes them as one shorthand, `font: 400 13.3333px Arial`; a font-family longhand restores the face but leaves size and leading. Width also requires rejecting `width: auto` and `width: fit-content`, even when readings match. Four failing classes and three excluded classes are pinned by name, so the derived count remains stable.

Layout. JSDOM computes no boxes, so shrink-to-fit is modelled with a width declaration. A row filling its line for another reason may look repaired.
The chrome itself. Stand-in values are Chromium’s, measured on the branch that created this gate and not updated afterward. A browser restyle would leave the stand-in stale.
Weight and style. `font: inherit` resets both, so rules preserving either must come after the shorthand; this gate does not read whether they do.
State. Readings are at rest, so chrome only shown on :hover is unseen.
Rows in its own ledger. A class rendered as a `<button>` is measured and counted rather than failed. Sixteen rows retain chrome nobody is repairing: twelve on text-align and four on line-height.
Deferred classes are measured in one ancestry each. Their rendering and ancestry counts are reported by the gate, not pinned. Other ancestries remain unmeasured.
Discovery starts at cursor: pointer. Moving that declaration can remove a class from discovery. Four failing subject classes are pinned by name.

The deliberate exclusion bucket: browser-owned form controls or their decoration, including the `select` behind .ui-select, the `label` around the checkbox in .ui-check and the `span` drawn by .ui-switch__track. prefers-color-scheme, which the kit does not ship. An unstamped document is dark on a light machine, and this gate treats that as intended (#250).

Pixels. JSDOM lays nothing out, so a 16px glyph is measured as a colour on a ground and as the declarations around its slot, never as a drawn mark. The React half. The rule is one kit declaration both faces load; React’s own tests match the class and the mark against its rendered tree, never the paint.
Accents other than the default. The other five redefine --glow-purple and are walked by the accent arm of the contrast ledger, not here.

A control a script adds after load. Nothing runs here.

GATES.does: Reads src/styles/tap-zone.css for the token, the pointer clause, a containing block per carrier, a real container per clearance, an !important on every opened gap, a clearance paired with every opening and a real entry per exemption; and, under TAP_ZONES=1, drives a browser over every story at 390 and 1280 sampling hit ownership with elementFromPoint along pixel-centre edges and an interior grid, so no control is drawn at a different size, the set of controls whose own box runs a different control does not grow, every named family reaches further, and a wider viewport or a mouse is untouched.

One engine and one theme. A pseudo-element on a form control is a browser behaviour, not a standard, and Firefox and Safari are not measured here.

Collisions are compared as a set of pairs rather than as coordinates, because opening a row’s gap moves the controls in it. A pair that merely moves to a different pixel of the same two controls is not reported.
Two controls whose drawn boxes already overlap are left out, so a layout defect that predates the zone is not reported as one the zone caused.

The one pixel two abutting controls share, where the neighbour's own drawn box reaches into that same pixel. Chromium awards it to one side by rounding — not a zone overreaching, and the same answer with the sheet off, for half of the sub-pixel offsets a panel can land on. Every other pixel centre a control holds is read, including one in a pixel it only partly covers, so an overreach smaller than that single shared pixel is unmeasured at such an edge and nothing else is. Two mutations hold both halves: a menu row's layer reaching a whole --tap-gap into the row beneath it, and a layer reaching 8.2px over a fractional edge, which an earlier whole-pixel sampling hid.

GATES.does: Reads the sheet for the eight declarations the file row’s layout depends on — the stack, the name line’s refusal to wrap, the stem’s ellipsis, the extension’s refusal to shrink, the facts tier’s refusal to wrap, the full-width track and the resting row’s floor — with a mutation per declaration, and checks that no container query or display:none has come back. Heights, widths, tier counts and line counts only: not colour, not the focus ring, and not whether a truncated stem still reads. The tier counts are a recorded table, not a derivation, so a state that gains or loses a tier fails here and is reviewed by hand.
One engine and one theme, and react/dist rather than the source.

The 150px name floor is asked only of a row at least 280px wide, because a guideline specimen nests its frame and panel inside Storybook’s stage and is narrower than the viewport it is measured at; the floor is therefore proved on the component’s own markup.
Four two-action shortfalls are accepted at recorded stem widths of 127px, 119px, 87px and 87px. The ledger rejects new or worse shortfalls.

GATES.name: Field ground
GATES.does: Walks every gallery under stories/components/ in both themes, composites the ground each field actually sits on, and checks that none of them is the page ground — a field paints --surface, so on the page it has no fill step and only --disabled-border left to be drawn by. Records the disabled text field's ground, fill, border, edge ratio and ink ratio per theme, and asserts its ink clears AA on the field's own paint. Mutations reject a page-ground field, an unchanged disabled edge, and a select left to browser fading. FIELD_PAINT=1 enables separate browser measurements of disabled field paint.
blind: The source half resolves declarations without layout or pixels. The optional browser half measures disabled fields in Chromium in both themes.
At rest only — hover, focus and active grounds belong to stories/contrast-dark.test.js and stories/contrast-light.test.js.
stories/components/ only: a guideline page's prose and a showcase's toolbar ground are those pages' decisions, not this gate's.

A contrast ratio is not legibility. The recorded edge readings are below the 3:1 non-text floor that WCAG 1.4.11 exempts a disabled control from, so they are recorded for review rather than asserted against a bar.

GATES.name: Field ground, React
GATES.does: The same rule as stories/field-ground.test.js over the React catalogue, off the same reading in stories/lib/field-ground.js. Discovers every story export of every *.stories.tsx under react/src without asking whether it can be rendered — CSF2's function form, a story's own render, the meta's, and `<component {...args} />` for an args-only one, over every component type React mounts — then mounts each in both themes, composites the ground each field actually sits on, and checks that none of them is the page ground. An export CSF leaves without a render is named rather than skipped, so a hole in the walk fails the coverage check instead of passing quietly. It also pins the field count, requires a disabled field and all five control kinds, and checks the body really carries --bg so a sheet that never loaded cannot buy a green run. Four mutations run that same discovery and mounting: a function-style story with a bare field, an args-only story of a forwardRef component, an export nothing can render, and Storybook's include/exclude rule.
blind: Historical browser captures, manual checks and browser measurements mentioned in this entry were not authenticated in this audit. They do not prove this head.
A story's render is called, so a decorator is not applied: a surface a decorator paints is unmeasured. This is why the kit's Card sits inside each render rather than in a decorator.
Storybook's args rendering is reproduced, not its real renderer. Loaders, play functions and argTypes are not run, so a field a play function puts on the page ground is unmeasured.
JSDOM reads winning declarations, not pixels: a rule inside a media query is unmeasured, and so is anything that depends on layout. The Chromium captures at 1280 and 390 in both themes cover paint.
At rest only, default accent — hover, focus and active grounds belong to react/src/contrast.test.tsx.
DOM ancestry stands in for visual stacking, so a field positioned over a non-ancestor reads the ground it descends from rather than the one drawn under it.

GATES.name: Stacked table rows
GATES.does: Renders every story that uses the stacked-table modifier and makes three checks on each stacked table it finds. That it names its table, row group, row, column header and cell roles in the markup, and still has a header row to clip, because a stylesheet cannot write a role. That nothing focusable is left in that clipped header, which can draw no focus ring. And that an order announced there by aria-sort has a focusable outside the table naming it in aria-controls, so the order can be changed by whoever is told about it.
blind: Historical browser captures, manual checks and browser measurements mentioned in this entry were not authenticated in this audit. They do not prove this head.
Markup is not speech: this reads attributes and cannot tell whether a screen reader announces a stacked row as a table, and it measures no layout, focus order or contrast.

How much the roles are worth was measured in one engine. In Chromium, stripping them leaves table, row, cell and columnheader standing and loses only the body's row group; WebKit and Gecko are unmeasured, so all five are required rather than the one engine shown to drop.

No story in the kit announces an order while stacked, so that check passes over the swept stories without judging one. It is held instead by the fixtures beside it, which keep unrelated focusables on the page: an earlier version asked only whether the page had a focusable at all, and passed the exact defect it was written to catch.

GATES.name: React: AccentPicker
GATES.does: Checks controlled accent selection, accessible names and pressed state, native keyboard activation, focus retention, form safety, SSR and host-owned persistence.
blind: JSDOM does not paint gradients, selection rings or focus indicators. Appearance and grid alignment need browser checks.

GATES.name: Rail strip hit area
GATES.does: Resolves rail widths in both themes from source CSS. Walks rendered descendants and rejects pointer-taking boxes wider than the folded strip. Checks inherited columns, min-width, subject counts and unchanged open widths. Width-changing boxes must use the rail transition timing or reject pointer input. Nine mutations test widths, pointer behavior and transition declarations.
blind: Historical browser captures, manual checks and browser measurements mentioned in this entry were not authenticated in this audit. They do not prove this head.
No layout, offsets or hit testing run here. Margins and transforms can move boxes outside the strip without failing the declared-width checks.

pointer-events has to be declared on the box that is past the strip. It is an inherited property and the cascade this gate reads does not inherit it, so an auto box inside a none one reads as auto. Conservative on purpose: the box past the strip is where the declaration belongs, and a reading that guessed would miss one that re-enabled the pointer.
A width this gate cannot fold into a length is a failure rather than a pass, except auto and 100%, which take the column of the box around them and are followed as such.
Anything a media query or a consumer's sheet does to the rail or the boxes inside it: only the rail's own rules and the ones the folded class adds are read.

The page shell's own folded rail (.ui-app__rail), whose rows keep the open column and which contains them with overflow: hidden auto. A different box with a different answer, and not this gate's subject — see #589.
Whether a row is big enough to hit, which is stories/tap-zone.test.js's question. This gate asks the opposite: whether anything claims a hit area it does not draw.
Transition duration, delay and easing are read as declarations. No animation frames are measured. Historical frame readings on #588 remain unverified here.

JSDOM does not expand the transition shorthand into its longhands, so the shorthand is parsed here. A sheet that wrote the longhands instead would read as no clock at all, which is a failure rather than a pass.

GATES.name: Phone shell controls
GATES.does: Measures the React phone band in Chromium at 320 and 390 with fine and coarse pointers. Checks the brand link, full accessible names, visible ellipsis, tap targets, viewport bounds, Dropdown panel hit testing, and native Tab and Shift+Tab in a shadow-root drawer. Checks the brand and reading column across 720 and 721.
blind: The source half reads only declarations and markup. The browser half needs PHONE_SHELL=1, a built Storybook and Playwright, so routine CI does not prove these measurements. Other consumer band controls are not measured.

GATES.name: Rail ring room
GATES.does: Resolves source CSS in JSDOM in both themes. Discovers rail rows whose outline matches a reference control. Checks row coverage, declared widths, and space for the outline through padding or an unclipped rail. Checks the border-box premise. Four failing mutations cover clipping, oversized rows, padding spent inside the rail, and unreadable percentage widths. A padded rail with narrower rows is a passing control.
blind: JSDOM resolves declared widths and outlines. Required clearance comes from ring-width and gap-width tokens, not computed outline-offset. Browser layout and pixels remain unmeasured.

Whether a row takes the ring at all, which is stories/focus-ring.test.js's question. This gate reads the rows that already draw it, and the row count it reconciles is what stops it passing over rows that lost it.

The column, not the outline. A row is measured against the width the rail lays it out in — its own width less padding and border — and the premise that the kit makes every box a border box is read off base.css and held by a test of its own, because JSDOM does not apply that universal rule.
Ancestors. A rail that clips nothing itself can still stand inside something that clips, and this gate asks the rail.
The shell rail is outside this gate. Historical shell-ring measurements reported on #575 are unverified here and do not prove the current head.
Anything a media query or a consumer's sheet does to the rail or its rows: only the rail's own rules and the ones the folded class adds are read.

GATES.name: A selected item's highlight
GATES.does: Reads selected-fill declarations from both workspaces and classifies every discovered rule. Measures ten subject selectors in both themes against named grounds at 1.1:1. These cover open and folded rails, three segmented spellings, dropdown rows and palette rows. Every declared background for each subject is checked. Mutations reject a flat fill, a later flat override, and a later removed fill. Subject and exclusion selectors must still exist.
blind: 1.1:1 is not a WCAG number and does not stand in for one: WCAG sets no contrast requirement for a background that carries no information by itself, and the ink ON these items is measured by stories/contrast-dark.test.js and stories/contrast-light.test.js instead. The grounds are named here rather than discovered, because which container an item ends up inside is not in the stylesheets; an item whose ground its own component does not fix — the pager, which stands on the page in one showcase and on a card in another — is a named exclusion and says so beside its rule.
The pager current-page mark is the only named exclusion. Its containing ground varies. Accent fills and rules that remove a fill are classified separately.

Nothing is laid out or painted: this reads declared values with the tokens substituted. It cannot see a fill covered by a pseudo-element, one a width query makes unreachable, or what any of them looks like on a real screen. A box painted WITHIN a selected item rather than being its mark — a count badge, an icon tile — is not discovered at all, because its marker sits on an ancestor compound.

GATES.name: Filter row: quiet edges and a text button
GATES.does: Discovers the chip and every data-filter wrapper, then reads each declared edge state and the states its primitive can paint. Chips and Add retain the chip edge at rest and on hover. Clear requires transparent edges in every state. Disabled chips and Add use the disabled edge, while keyboard focus uses the accent. Missing subjects, missing states, unknown states and weaker overrides fail. Eighteen mutations prove rejection.
blind: Paint. It reads the sheets' declarations by selector and specificity, not pixels. The Chromium measurements at 1280 and 390 in both themes, at rest, hovered, focused, with the catalogue open and with the row off, cover what is drawn.

An !important, an inline style, a consumer override and an @media block are not read, so an edge overridden in one of those is uncovered. A neighbour is discovered only where this sheet names its attribute: one a consumer draws from its own sheet is outside the gate.

Which of two carriers of one state matches a real element. A bar turned off does not set :disabled on a nested fieldset, so the chip is required to take its unavailable edge both from its own state and from the bar's, rather than measured as doing so; the browser captures show which one paints.
Contrast. It checks which token is drawn, not what that edge measures against the fill behind it; the contrast walk and the accessibility floor own those numbers.
Whether :focus-visible matches on a real keystroke, and whether the ring is visible once it does. The focus-ring gates and the browser captures own both.

UNGATED.note: Keyboard gates cover segmented controls, tabs, dropdowns, palettes, overlays and several React flows. They do not prove browser Tab order through every shell rail or consumer composition. Each gate states its scope above.
The contrast gate calls this its largest single gap. Only a real browser closes it (#131).
